ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure labels adenosine binding to G protein-coupled receptor, and there is G protein beside the receptor; the figure shows the exchange of GDP and GTP, and a G protein subunit bound to GTP is located beside adenylyl cyclase (AC). AC is labeled as “active”, and its downstream arrow shows ATP converting to cAMP. Reasoning: Because in the figure the G protein subunit bound to GTP is connected to AC labeled as active, and leads to cAMP generation, after GTP binds to the G protein subunit it will activate adenylyl cyclase.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram labels and arrows: the image shows a G protein coupled receptor, a G protein that exchanges GDP for GTP, and adenylyl cyclase (AC) marked as active downstream of the GTP-bound G protein, with cAMP production indicated. Then apply the pathway rule that GTP binding activates the G protein subunit, which in turn activates AC. Therefore the answer is Yes.
